title: Documentary Proof Threshold
policy_text: Claims over SGD 20 need an itemised receipt showing the date, vendor, and what was purchased -- a total-only receipt is not enough once you're over SGD 20. Claims of SGD 20 or less don't need itemised proof; your own written description at the time of the claim is enough. This SGD 20 limit applies per transaction, not per reporting period, and doesn't override the other eligibility rules elsewhere in this policy document. If the receipt is illegible, cropped, or otherwise unclear, follow the Indeterminate Documentary Detail policy (POL-16) instead of treating it as if no receipt was provided at all.

title: Staff Sustenance Allowance
policy_text: You can claim your own meals only when: (a) you're on an approved trip away from your normal workplace, (b) you've worked significantly beyond normal hours with a documented reason, or (c) another clearly documented work reason applies. The cap is SGD 40 per person per meal occasion, regardless of how many items are on the bill. If several colleagues eat together with no external client present, the SGD 40 cap applies per person, not per bill. This is different from client hospitality (POL-03), which has a higher cap for a different purpose. An ordinary working day at your usual workplace, with no extended hours and no other documented reason, does not qualify at all. Finance may ask for your itinerary or timesheet to confirm eligibility where it isn't otherwise obvious.

title: Customer Hospitality (Dining)
policy_text: When you host an external client or business contact for a meal for a genuine business reason, you can claim up to SGD 150 per person, including yourself. To claim under this policy, your submission must state two things: (1) who the external contact is (their name or organisation), and (2) the business reason for the meal -- for example an account review, a contract negotiation, or a relationship-building discussion tied to real or prospective business. If either of these is missing, the claim cannot be assessed under this policy and will be sent back to you for the missing detail. If alcohol was served, see POL-04 for extra conditions that apply on top of this policy. Any amount per person above SGD 150 is not reimbursable -- you cover the difference personally, or it comes from a separate pre-agreed budget line outside this policy.

title: Intoxicating Beverages
policy_text: Alcohol is not reimbursable, with one narrow exception: alcohol served as part of a qualifying client hospitality meal under POL-03 -- where the client's identity and business reason are documented and the rest of the meal is otherwise compliant -- can be claimed. Alcohol at an ordinary staff meal under POL-02 is never reimbursable, even when shared only among colleagues. Even for a qualifying client meal, Finance can still query a bill where alcohol makes up an unusually large share of the total, and a pattern of alcohol-heavy claims may be sent to a manager for review regardless of whether each individual claim is technically compliant. This policy only ever applies on top of an otherwise-valid client hospitality claim under POL-03 -- it is never a standalone way to claim alcohol on its own.

title: Ground Conveyance for Work Journeys
policy_text: Taxi, ride-hailing, and similar hired ground transport is reimbursable for genuine work travel -- between offices, to or from a client site, or to or from a transport terminal for an approved trip. Ordinary commuting between your home and your normal workplace is never reimbursable under this or any other policy, regardless of the transport mode or time of day, except for the narrow after-hours exception in POL-06. Choose the most cost-effective reasonable option available at the time; Finance may query a much more expensive premium option when a standard one was readily available. If a single trip mixes personal and work purposes, only claim the work portion of the fare -- see POL-15 for how to record a split like this.

title: After-Hours Conveyance
policy_text: As a narrow exception to the rule that ordinary commuting isn't reimbursable, transport directly from your workplace to home is reimbursable if your working day ends at or after 22:00. This exists because of reduced public transport options and safety considerations late at night. To claim this, you must record the specific operational reason your day ran that late -- for example a critical deadline, a call scheduled to align with another time zone, or an unplanned incident. If your day ended before 22:00, this exception does not apply, even if the day felt unusually demanding to you. This is separate from POL-05, which covers ordinary daytime work travel and still applies regardless of the hour.

title: Work-Related Lodging
policy_text: Hotel stays for an approved work trip are reimbursable up to SGD 300 per night, including standard taxes and service charges. Minibar use, laundry, and other incidental charges are never reimbursable under any policy in this document. If the nightly rate exceeds SGD 300 -- because of location, availability, or the standard of room booked -- the excess needs your supervisor's documented authorisation obtained BEFORE the booking is confirmed. Without that prior authorisation, the excess is disallowed regardless of the reason, except in genuinely exceptional cases at Finance's discretion. Book through the company's designated channels where available, since these usually offer rates below the cap and make reconciliation easier.

title: Air Travel Cabin Class
policy_text: The default reimbursable airfare class for an approved work trip is economy, or the carrier's most basic fare class. Any higher class -- premium economy, business, or first -- needs your supervisor's documented authorisation obtained BEFORE the booking is made. Authorisation obtained after the booking is already confirmed is not accepted, except in genuinely exceptional circumstances at Finance's discretion, such as an urgent operational need with no time for prior sign-off. Factors that can support pre-authorisation for a higher class include a long flight duration, documented medical needs, or the standard class being unavailable for the required dates. You are responsible for obtaining and submitting proof of pre-authorisation together with your fare confirmation.

title: Private Acquisitions
policy_text: Personal purchases -- items or services that mainly benefit you personally rather than the business -- are never reimbursable, regardless of the circumstances in which they were bought. This applies even when a personal item appears on the same receipt as an otherwise-eligible business item; in that case only the business portion may be claimed (see POL-15 for how to record the split). Describing a personal item in business-sounding terms does not change what it actually is. If your description does not appear to match what is actually shown on the receipt, that mismatch should be handled under the receipt/description-mismatch guidance rather than assessed under this policy alone, since a mismatch like this can itself be a sign of trying to claim a personal item as a business cost.

title: Workplace Apparatus
policy_text: Equipment you genuinely need to do your job -- computer peripherals, ergonomic furniture, and similar tools of the role -- is reimbursable when there is a clear, stated operational need for it. A single item costing more than SGD 200 needs your supervisor's documented authorisation, kept together with the claim. This SGD 200 limit applies per item, not per submission -- several genuinely separate items each under SGD 200 do not need authorisation even if they add up to more than SGD 200 in total, as long as they really are separate items and not one higher-value purchase artificially split into line items to avoid this rule. Equipment bought under this policy remains company property, even where it is kept at your usual workplace or an agreed remote location. This policy covers physical tools of the role; for recurring digital-tool subscriptions, see POL-11 instead.

title: Digital Tool Access Fees
policy_text: Recurring fees for digital tools or online services you need for work, usually billed monthly, are reimbursable up to SGD 50 per month, provided you record the business justification with your first claim for that tool. If it is an annual or other longer-term commitment, or the monthly-equivalent cost is more than SGD 50, you need your supervisor's documented authorisation BEFORE entering into the commitment or making the first payment. This policy covers ongoing subscriptions, not a one-off purchase of software under a perpetual licence -- that should instead be claimed as equipment under POL-10. Cancel a subscription promptly once you no longer need it; the company keeps paying for it for as long as it remains active.

title: Goodwill Tokens
policy_text: A goodwill gift to an external business contact -- for example, marking a significant milestone in a business relationship -- is reimbursable up to SGD 100 in value, provided you record who received it and the business reason for it at the time of the claim. Cash, or anything easily converted to cash such as gift cards or vouchers usable broadly, is never reimbursable as a goodwill gift, at any value, because it is difficult to show that it served a genuine relationship-building purpose rather than being a disguised payment. Gifts to colleagues inside the company are not covered by this policy at all and are generally a personal matter for you, unless a separate, specifically authorised staff-recognition budget applies, which sits outside this document.

title: Non-Home Denomination Claims
policy_text: If an expense was paid in a currency other than the company's home currency, record it in your claim exactly as shown on the original receipt -- in that original currency and amount -- and do not convert it yourself. Finance converts the eligible amount to the home currency centrally, using the company's standard exchange-rate process for around the date the expense was incurred, rather than whatever rate your card issuer or currency exchange actually charged you. All the other eligibility rules elsewhere in this document still fully apply to a foreign-currency expense -- this policy only governs how the figure is recorded and converted, and creates no separate exemption or extra entitlement.

title: Non-Working Day Costs
policy_text: An expense on a weekend or a public holiday is not automatically excluded from reimbursement, but you must state, at the time of submission, the specific operational reason the expense had to happen on that particular day rather than during the ordinary working week. A general statement that the work was 'important' or 'urgent', without more detail, does not satisfy this requirement -- name the actual concrete reason, such as an event that could only be held that day, or a deadline on the following working day that required preparation over the weekend. Whatever policy normally applies to that category of expense still applies on top of this rule -- a weekend or holiday claim must satisfy both this policy and the specific policy governing that category of expense.

title: Combined Proof-of-Purchase
policy_text: If a single receipt or invoice covers both a genuine business cost and one or more personal items, you can still claim the business portion -- a personal item on the same document does not disqualify the business part, as long as the two can be clearly told apart. You must state which specific line items are the business ones and the resulting amount you are claiming, rather than submitting the combined total and leaving Finance to work out the split. If the document does not itemise clearly enough to support this, give a reasonable estimate together with an explanation of your basis for it; Finance can query a split that looks disproportionate to the description given. This policy works alongside POL-09 (personal items are never reimbursable on their own) -- it exists specifically for the common case where business and personal items land on the same receipt.

title: Indeterminate Documentary Detail
policy_text: If a detail essential to assessing a claim -- the total amount, the date, or the vendor's identity -- cannot be confidently read from the supporting documentation, whether because it is faded, cropped, damaged, or otherwise unclear, the claim must not be assessed using an assumed or guessed value for that detail. Instead, send the submission back to the employee for clarification if it is something they can reasonably be expected to confirm, or escalate it to Finance Review for manual determination if the detail cannot be reliably established even with the employee's input, or if its absence raises a broader doubt about the reliability of the whole submission. This reflects a rule that runs throughout this document: never guess a figure, date, or other material fact in order to reach a decision, however plausible the guess might seem.

title: External Learning and Gatherings
policy_text: Fees to enrol in an external course, programme, or professional event are reimbursable only where: (1) the actual content is genuinely relevant to your current duties or to a role you are actively being prepared for, and (2) your supervisor's documented authorisation was obtained and recorded BEFORE you enrolled. Judge relevance by the programme's actual content, not just its general subject area -- a programme broadly in your field but not addressing your actual responsibilities may still fail this requirement. Cancellation or no-show fees from missing an otherwise-authorised programme are not reimbursable except in genuinely exceptional circumstances, such as a documented illness reported within the provider's cancellation window. Claim travel and lodging for attending such a programme separately under the relevant travel and accommodation policies, rather than bundling them into this enrolment-fee claim.

title: Vehicle Standing and Road-Usage Charges
policy_text: Parking charges and toll or road-usage fees are reimbursable when incurred during a genuine work journey, on the same basis the underlying journey itself would be reimbursable under POL-05. Fines and penalty notices of any kind -- parking tickets, moving-traffic violations, or any other regulatory penalty -- are never reimbursable under this or any other policy, regardless of the circumstances or whether the underlying journey was itself legitimate business travel; the company does not cover the cost of regulatory non-compliance. If you use your own car for a work journey instead of hired transport, charges of this kind remain reimbursable the same way, but the vehicle's own running costs are handled separately under the mileage policy, POL-21.

title: Non-Dining Customer Hospitality
policy_text: Client hospitality that is not a shared meal -- event tickets, venue admission, or a similar experience offered in a commercial relationship-building context -- requires three things to be recorded BEFORE the expense is incurred, not after the fact: (1) who the client contact is or which organisation they represent, (2) the business reason for the occasion, and (3) your supervisor's documented pre-authorisation. This need for advance approval, rather than after-the-fact justification, is what distinguishes this policy from client dining under POL-03, reflecting the typically higher and less predictable cost of experiences covered here. If you did not get pre-authorisation before the event, you cannot fix this afterwards -- the claim does not qualify under this policy at all, no matter how strong the business justification looks in hindsight.

title: Service Levies and Gratuities
policy_text: A compulsory service charge added to a bill is reimbursable on the same basis as the underlying cost it is attached to -- if that underlying cost is not itself eligible, the service charge on it is not reimbursable either. A voluntary tip beyond any compulsory charge is reimbursable up to one-tenth (10%) of the qualifying amount it relates to, calculated before the tip itself is added. A voluntary tip above that 10% needs a written explanation from you at the time of submission, covering the circumstance that justified going above the usual proportion, such as an unusually large group or exceptional service under difficult conditions. This policy is always tied to whichever policy governs the underlying expense -- a service charge or tip can never be more eligible than the cost it accompanies.

title: Personal Vehicle Mileage
policy_text: If you use a personally owned vehicle for an approved work journey instead of hired transport or public transport, you can claim a mileage-based allowance instead of actual fuel or running costs, calculated at the standard per-kilometre rate Finance publishes from time to time. This rate is meant to cover fuel, wear, and incidental running costs together -- you cannot also separately claim fuel or servicing for the same journey. Ordinary commuting between your home and your usual workplace is still excluded, on the same basis as under POL-05, regardless of which vehicle or mode you use for it. Keep a simple record of the origin, destination, and distance of each trip in case the claim is queried.

title: Relocation Assistance
policy_text: If the company requires you to relocate your main residence to take up a role at a different office location, reasonable relocation costs directly tied to that move are reimbursable, but only under a separate written agreement made with you BEFORE the move takes place, setting out exactly what is covered and any applicable cap. Without that written agreement, no cost associated with a change of residence is reimbursable under this or any other policy, regardless of whether the move was connected to your employment. Costs typically covered include the physical transport of household belongings and short-term temporary accommodation bridging the move, but exclude personal or discretionary costs such as buying new furnishings. This policy is administered separately from the general expense-reimbursement process described elsewhere in this document.

title: Home Office Equipment Stipend
policy_text: If your home has been formally agreed as your workplace, in whole or in part, you may claim a one-off stipend toward setting up a suitable home working environment, up to a limit set and periodically reviewed by Human Resources. This stipend is separate from, and cannot be combined with, the workplace-apparatus provisions in POL-10 -- the same item cannot be claimed under both policies. Eligible items are limited to what is genuinely needed for a functional, ergonomically appropriate workspace -- such as a desk, a chair, or suitable lighting -- and exclude general household items unrelated to the immediate working area. This stipend is available once per employee per home-working arrangement, not on a recurring basis, unless your role or working arrangement changes materially.

title: Professional Body Membership
policy_text: Annual membership fees for a recognised professional body directly relevant to your role are reimbursable once your supervisor's documented authorisation confirms the relevance of that body to your duties. This is different from POL-17, which covers one-off enrolment fees for courses and events rather than ongoing membership -- a professional body's own conferences or courses, where separately charged, should be assessed under POL-17 instead. If a membership confers a personal professional qualification that continues to benefit you after you leave the company, Finance may take that into account in deciding whether, and how much, to reimburse, though this does not by itself disqualify an otherwise-eligible membership.

title: Mobile Communications Allowance
policy_text: If your role genuinely requires regular use of your personal mobile device for work, you can claim a fixed monthly allowance toward the associated costs, at a rate set separately by Finance, instead of itemising your actual phone bill. If you already have a company-issued device and plan, you cannot also claim this allowance for the same period, since the underlying need is already met. This allowance covers ordinary voice, messaging, and data use connected to your duties -- it does not cover buying the handset itself, which should instead be assessed under POL-10 (workplace apparatus) where there is a genuine business need.

title: Staff Wellness Benefit
policy_text: A discretionary annual allowance toward activities supporting your general wellbeing, such as fitness memberships or similar activities, may be available under a separate benefits schedule maintained by Human Resources, which sets the applicable cap and eligible categories from time to time. This benefit is administered outside the general expense-reimbursement process in this document and should not be claimed through the same channel as an ordinary business expense -- refer to the separate benefits schedule for the correct process. For the avoidance of doubt, costs under this benefit are not business expenses within the meaning of this document, even though they may be processed through a similar-looking mechanism.

title: Team Offsite Events
policy_text: Costs for an organised offsite event for your immediate team -- venue hire, catering, and related activities -- are reimbursable where the event was authorised in advance by a manager at or above department-head level, and a per-head budget for the event was agreed before it took place. Costs materially exceeding that agreed per-head budget need further authorisation at the same level BEFORE they are incurred, not justified after the event. This policy applies instead of, not in addition to, POL-02 (staff meals) and POL-03 (client hospitality) for an event that qualifies as a team offsite under this policy.

title: Charitable Contribution Matching
policy_text: If you make a personal donation to a registered charity, the company may match it up to an annual per-employee cap, through a separate charitable-matching scheme run by Human Resources rather than through the general expense-reimbursement process. Submit a matching request together with evidence of your donation, within the timeframe the scheme specifies; it is assessed against the scheme's own eligibility rules, not this document. This entry is included here for completeness only and is not part of the expense-reimbursement provisions administered by Finance.

title: Extended Trip Per Diem
policy_text: For an approved trip away from your usual base that spans more than one calendar day, you may choose to claim sustenance on a flat daily rate instead of itemising each meal separately, at a daily figure set separately by Finance for that destination. Once you make this choice for a trip, you cannot also claim individual meals under POL-02 for the same days of that trip -- the two approaches are mutually exclusive for the same period. This flat-rate option is only available where the trip genuinely spans more than one calendar day; a single-day trip, however long, should be claimed under the ordinary POL-02 meal rules instead. You do not need itemised meal receipts for days claimed this way, but you still need evidence that the travel itself took place.

title: Large-Group Client Hospitality
policy_text: Where a client dining occasion has more than six attendees in total, including you and the counterparts, the normal per-head cap for customer hospitality under POL-03 still applies, but you additionally need documented pre-authorisation from a manager at or above department-head level before the occasion takes place. This extra requirement reflects the materially higher total cost such occasions can represent and the greater need for oversight before the commitment is made. Where the group size could not reasonably have been anticipated at booking time -- for example, additional counterparts joined without advance notice -- Finance may accept the claim without prior authorisation, provided the circumstances are clearly explained in the submission. This policy applies in addition to, not instead of, POL-03, which continues to govern the underlying per-head eligibility and the recording of the counterpart's identity and business reason.

title: Specialised Technical Equipment
policy_text: Specialised or technical equipment -- going beyond the ordinary computing peripherals and furniture covered by POL-10, and instead comprising equipment specific to a particular technical function such as laboratory instruments or specialised measurement devices -- has a higher authorisation threshold of SGD 500 instead of the general SGD 200 figure, reflecting the more specialised procurement judgement such equipment typically needs. If you are unsure whether an item falls under this specialised category rather than the general provisions, check with your supervisor before purchase; Finance's own determination at the point the claim is assessed is final. Authorisation for equipment under this policy should come from a supervisor with relevant technical or budgetary oversight of the function in question, rather than automatically your direct line manager if they do not hold that oversight.

title: Internal Certification Programmes
policy_text: Enrolling in a certification or training programme delivered internally by the company's own Learning and Development function, as distinct from an external provider, does not require the supervisor authorisation that POL-17 requires for external programmes, since internal programmes are already understood to be curated for relevance to roles within the company. You should still register your enrolment through the designated internal system where one exists, though this is an administrative step rather than a condition of eligibility. If an internally delivered programme carries an associated cost payable to a third party -- for example, an external facilitator engaged to deliver an otherwise-internal programme -- that cost should be assessed under POL-17 instead of this policy, since the third-party cost element takes it outside the scope of a purely internal programme.

title: Long-Term Parking Arrangements
policy_text: If your role genuinely requires frequent enough use of parking facilities at one location that a season pass or other long-term arrangement would be more cost-effective than repeated single-use charges, that arrangement is reimbursable with your supervisor's documented authorisation of the underlying operational need, obtained BEFORE you enter into the arrangement. This is different from POL-18, which covers single-use parking and toll charges on a per-journey basis -- a long-term arrangement entered into without the authorisation this policy requires should instead be assessed, if at all, under POL-18, and only to the extent individual journeys can actually be evidenced. Discontinue a long-term arrangement promptly once the underlying operational need no longer exists, rather than letting it continue by default.

title: Extended-Stay Accommodation
policy_text: For a work trip requiring lodging for a continuous period of more than seven nights at the same location, you should, wherever practicable, seek an extended-stay or similar longer-term accommodation arrangement rather than continuing to book on a standard nightly basis, since such arrangements typically secure a materially lower effective nightly rate. The SGD 300 nightly cap from POL-07 still applies, but to the effective nightly rate of the extended-stay arrangement -- calculated by dividing the total arrangement cost by the number of nights covered -- rather than to any single night in isolation. If you keep booking on a standard nightly basis throughout a stay of more than seven nights when an extended-stay option was reasonably available, Finance may query the claim for not pursuing the more cost-effective option.

title: Ride-Sharing and Pooled Transport
policy_text: Where two or more employees travelling to the same destination for the same work purpose share a single hired ground conveyance, the fare should be claimed once by a single nominated employee among the group and apportioned or reimbursed internally between the travelling colleagues, rather than each colleague separately claiming the full fare. This policy exists to avoid duplicate reimbursement of what is, in substance, a single shared journey. Where colleagues genuinely cannot share a single conveyance because of divergent onward destinations or timing, each may claim separately under POL-05 as normal, and this policy does not apply. If you do share a ride under this policy, note in your submission the names of the colleagues you shared it with, so Finance can match it against any related claims from the same journey.
